caption: The drawing depicts a single, symmetrical, flower-shaped object centered on a plain, light beige background. The object consists of a central circular part covered with a crisscross grid pattern, surrounded by eight rounded, petal-like segments. Each petal segment is three-dimensionally rendered with shading that gives them depth, and they are depicted as hollowed or concave, with each one showing internal grooves and variations in color. The color palette of the object is primarily earthy tones, such as brown, tan, muted green, and hints of gray, with areas showing lighter highlights and darker shadows to suggest wear or texture. The flower shape appears to be carved or sculpted, with irregularities in the surface. In the lower right corner of the drawing, the name "Clayton Clement" and the abbreviation "N.C.W.A." are written in small, neat black text.
title: Wood Carving - Flower
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
